turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My dad died two months ago. Today I found his gardening gloves in the shed and I just sat there.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Finding his gloves must have brought him close again, and left you sitting with a lot all at once. I’m glad you told me. What was going through your mind as you sat there?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I kept thinking he’d be back to get them. He used to call me every Sunday, too. I still catch myself waiting for the phone to ring.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You still find yourself expecting the Sunday call, as if some part of you hasn’t caught up with how much has changed. That sounds so painful. I’m glad you told me about him. What were your Sunday calls usually like?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We’d talk about nothing much. His garden, the weather. Sometimes he’d ask if I was eating properly. I miss how ordinary it was.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It’s the ordinary little things you miss—the garden, the weather, him checking that you were eating. Those calls were a steady part of your life, and it makes sense that their absence hurts. What do Sundays feel like for you now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They feel too quiet. And I’m still not speaking to my brother. We argued at the funeral about selling the house. I miss Dad, and I hate that this is what we’re left with.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You’re carrying the quiet of Sundays and the hurt with your brother, all while missing your dad. It’s painful when a funeral argument becomes part of what’s left behind. Reaching out here and putting that into words is a real effort. What feels hardest about the distance with your brother right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep thinking we were both grieving and just made it worse. But I don’t know how to reach out without starting the house argument again. The gloves made me think Dad would’ve hated us being like this.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: The gloves brought up how much you miss your dad, and how painful it feels to be distant from your brother while you’re both grieving. You don’t have to solve the house question just to open a small door between you. Would a simple message about missing him and wanting to talk, without discussing the house yet, feel possible?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I’m not ready to send anything tonight. I just miss Dad so much.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You don’t have to send anything tonight. You miss your dad, and finding those gloves has made that loss feel especially close. I’m glad you’re letting yourself say it here. What do you miss most about him right now?
